title: Let the seat store change maps without its callers noticing

blocks.text: The ticketing service keeps seat holds in `SeatHolds`. The box office shares one store between its request threads, so it gets a `ConcurrentHashMap`; the overnight re-seating tool runs on one thread over a `TreeMap`; the tests use a `HashMap`. The callers never see which: they get a store from `shared()`, `sorted()` or `plain()` and call its methods.

Last month a bug reached production that every test had passed: code that worked over the `HashMap` failed in the box office. Make sure that can't happen again. Finish the three `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/SeatHolds.java`:

items: `hold(seat, guest)`: the guest now holds the seat;
`holder(seat)`: who holds the seat, if anyone;

blocks.text: When you're done, a caller that works with one of the three stores works the same way with the other two, including when it passes `null` and when it changes the store while walking the list it got from `holds()`. `release` is already written. About four lines in total.

cases.says: holding, replacing, looking up, releasing and listing seats give the same results over a HashMap, a TreeMap and a ConcurrentHashMap
a hold with no guest throws NullPointerException over every map, including one that would store a null, and changes nothing
asking who holds a null seat throws NullPointerException over every map, including one that would answer it
the list of holds is a copy: walking it while the store changes neither throws nor shows the changes, over every map

origin.section: The Swap Is Free Only for What the Wrapper Promises: HashMap Accepted null, ConcurrentHashMap Throws

concepts: Callers that use only a wrapper's methods keep working, unchanged and uncompiled, when the map it keeps privately changes from HashMap to ConcurrentHashMap, and the shared-map races end.
Map implementations differ on null, so a wrapper keeps its callers independent of the map only if it decides about null itself, failing the same way over every backing.
A wrapper that returns its live map or a view hands callers the backing's own iterator behaviour; returning a copy keeps it the same over every backing.
